name: Windigo
description: A spirit-being of Algonquian-language traditions — Ojibwe wiindigoo, Cree wīhtikōw — embodying the moral horror of cannibalism, of insatiable greed, and of the heart turned to ice. Both a being met in story and a name for a culturally specific psychological transformation.

aliases.name: Wendigo
aliases.meaning: Anglicised form popularised by Algernon Blackwood (1910)

aliases.name: Wechuge
aliases.meaning: Closely related but distinct cannibal-spirit figure

origin: The Windigo is a being of the boreal forest of northern North America, associated specifically with the territories of Algonquian-speaking peoples — Ojibwe / Anishinaabe, Cree, Innu, Naskapi, Atikamekw, Saulteaux — across present-day Canada and the northern United States.
